source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is pursuing backward integration into KSMs/APIs (own manufacturing, PIC/S-approved API plant, ~Rs 290.7 cr organic capex in Q3FY25, funded partly via a Rs 5,000 cr QIP) to reduce its own dependence on imported Chinese APIs/intermediates. This is framed as supply-chain security/self-reliance for Zydus's own inputs, not as a 'customers diversifying away from China to Zydus' export-growth narrative, so it does not meet the 'moderate/strong' bar.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Treasury policy combines natural hedges (USD receivables vs USD payables) with forward contracts/options; public disclosures suggest ~40-70% coverage of near-term known FX exposure (not an exact AR-quoted figure).
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment revenue mix: US Formulations 31.0%, India Formulations 21.8%, Consumer Wellness 17.9% (mostly domestic), International Markets Formulations 13.8%, Other 15.8% (API/animal health, largely export). US$2.75bn total FY25 revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Zydus is not named among the major disclosed beneficiaries of the Bulk Drugs/KSM PLI scheme (Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Lupin, Cipla, Intas, Torrent are the companies commonly cited as having expanded capacity under it); no company-specific PLI disbursement or certification for Zydus was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a domestic diagnostics/pathology chain (with minor cross-border lab presence in Nepal/Bangladesh); it has no manufacturing export business, so a China+1 supply-chain narrative is not applicable.

rural.evidence: FY25 annual report/MD&A emphasizes expansion into Tier-3 and Tier-4 markets (18 new labs added in FY25) as a strategic growth driver, alongside sample volume growth of 9.5% to 20.9 million and patient volume growth of 3.8% to 6.8 million. No explicit % of revenue from rural/Tier-3-4 markets was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Diagnostics/pathology services is not a sector covered by any PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: The dominant China-related narrative found is a supply-chain RISK (China's export restrictions on heavy rare-earth magnets used in EV traction motors), which Sona Comstar addressed by redesigning motors to use light rare-earth-magnet or magnet-free alternatives, and by broader diversification 'across products, platforms and geographies' to reduce concentration risk. Order book of ~INR 237-242 bn (~70% EV-linked, 67 EV programmes across 35 customers, 60+ OEMs/Tier-1s) reflects customer/geography diversification, but this is not framed in the AR as customers shifting sourcing away from China to India (i.e., not a classic China+1 export-tailwind narrative), so strength is kept at 'weak' rather than moderate/strong.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Consolidated financials show a 'Cash Flow Hedge Reserve' and 'Foreign currency translation reserve' in equity, and a 'Fair value loss/(gain) on derivatives' of INR 25.63 mn (FY24-25), indicating active use of forward/derivative hedging; exact hedge ratio not disclosed in accessible sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: By region: India ~41% of revenue, North America ~30%, Europe ~24% (most recent disclosed geographic split, from Q2FY26/FY25-adjacent investor materials since the exact FY25 AR segment table wasn't directly accessible). Company operates plants in India, China, Mexico and USA.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first auto-component supplier in India to receive Auto PLI (Production Linked Incentive) certification, for its hub-wheel-drive motor for electric two-wheelers; company has filed 7 applications for different products under the Auto PLI scheme. Revenue contribution/incentive amount not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: NFIL's agrochemical intermediates business (80-90% of divisional output) sells directly to the top-5 global innovator agrochemical companies and major Japanese firms via long-term, innovator-linked contracts (not generic/commodity), positioned explicitly against 'Chinese chemical manufacturers... aggressively dumping generic agrochemical intermediates... at dirt-cheap prices.' Investor/analyst commentary widely attributes NFIL's export-led growth to 'China+1 sentiment' and 'rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers'; company has also de-risked fluorspar (key raw material, China-dominated supply) via long-term contracts with South African miners, with Chinese production expected to phase down further from CY29. FY25 export contribution was ~77% of revenue (Q4FY25 figure).

crude_exposure.evidence: Navin Fluorine's chemistry is fluorine/fluorspar-based (not petroleum-derived), so direct crude-oil raw-material linkage was not found; no evidence of material crude exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment revenue: HPP (refrigerants/HFO) ~51.3% (Rs 1,206 cr), Specialty Chemicals ~34.1% (Rs 800 cr), CDMO ~14.6% (Rs 343 cr); export contribution ~77% of revenue in Q4FY25, indicating heavy USD-denominated export exposure. Specific forward-contract hedging ratio not found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI scheme for the specialty chemicals sector has been under development/consideration by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers; no confirmation was found that Navin Fluorine has been certified as or disbursed funds as a beneficiary under any PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Radico is an India-focused IMFL (Indian Made Foreign Liquor) manufacturer; exports (~8-9% of revenue, ~4-5% of volume, to 85-100+ countries) are being diversified partly due to US tariff pressure, but there is no China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative relevant to this business.

rural.evidence: FY25 MD&A highlights premiumisation (Prestige & Above, P&A) as the primary growth driver, with P&A revenue share rising from 40% (FY20) to 48% (FY25) and 46% of IMFL volumes / 69.4% of IMFL value in FY25. Separately, 'Regular' (mass-market/semi-urban-rural-skewed) segment volumes rebounded sharply from Q3FY25 after nine consecutive quarters of decline, contributing meaningfully to full-year growth -- indicating a rural/mass-market demand recovery, but no explicit % of revenue from rural markets was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt ~Rs 868 cr as of Mar-25 (up from ~Rs 749 cr as of Mar-24); company described as having a low cost of borrowing due to a favorable interest-rate environment, stable profitability and strong capital structure. No floating-rate liability % disclosed in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Packaging inputs (notably PET bottles) are petroleum-derived, so rising crude oil prices and a weaker rupee increase import costs for packaging materials; recent cost inflation cited includes glass bottles up ~20% and paper cartons up ~100%. Core alcohol feedstock (grain/molasses-based ENA) is not crude-linked; company commissioned a 350 KLPD distillery at Sitapur in FY25 partly to secure long-term ENA supply. No raw-material % tied to crude was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are a small share of revenue (~8-9%), so INR/USD exposure is limited relative to the other companies in this batch.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages is not a PLI-covered sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary sources (BW People, Business Standard, Electronics For You) report LG is relocating some capital-goods production to India from Korea/China/Vietnam and investing ~Rs 5,000 crore in a new Sri City plant explicitly framed as supply-chain diversification, targeting a rise in export share from ~6-7% toward ~14% of sales and supplying 50-60+ countries. Company cited 'geographical diversification' as a lever to manage rupee depreciation and raw-material cost risk. Not confirmed via direct AR MD&A text read (search snippets only).

rural.evidence: Company has introduced a value-tier 'Essential Series' explicitly targeting Tier-2/Tier-3 and rural markets, backed by 96 regional offices and 35,000+ retail touchpoints; management expects it to reach ~10% of product mix within 1-1.5 years, but no revenue % from rural markets is disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw materials (steel, copper, aluminium, polymers/resins incl. ABS & EPS, semiconductors, electromechanical parts) were ~75.25% of revenue from operations in FY25 (71.46% FY24, 75.07% FY23) per RHP/annual disclosures. ABS/EPS resins are crude-oil derivatives but no specific petrochemical/crude-linked % is broken out separately.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company explicitly names rupee depreciation as a margin risk, managed partly via geographic diversification and a stronger B2B portfolio; no specific hedging policy or USD revenue % was found in reachable sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: LG Electronics was among the firms provisionally selected as a beneficiary under India's PLI Scheme for White Goods (ACs & LED lights), with reported AC-components committed investment of ~Rs 1,368 crore (compressors, copper tubes, heat exchangers, BLDC motors). No revenue-linked incentive amount or % disclosed in sources reached.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Government of India PSU (Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas); primary clients are PSUs (IOCL, BPCL) plus central/state government bodies (e.g. ~Rs 245 crore contracts from Maharashtra & West Bengal state governments), spanning petroleum refining, oil & gas, pipelines, petrochemicals, infrastructure, water & waste management, and green hydrogen. FY25: order book at all-time high Rs 11,700 crore (vs Rs 7,823 crore FY24), order inflow Rs 8,214 crore (vs Rs 3,400 crore FY24); consultancy revenue ~Rs 1,782 crore and turnkey ~Rs 2,068 crore (total income ~Rs 4,059 crore). Effectively the large majority of revenue is government/PSU-capex linked, but no single consolidated % figure was disclosed in sources reached.

rate_sensitive.evidence: EIL is a net-cash, effectively debt-free PSU (cash & liquid funds ~Rs 1,115 crore as of Sep-2025; net cash ~Rs 1,250 crore); working capital is funded from accruals/liquid funds, so floating-rate liability exposure appears negligible.

inr_exposure.evidence: EIL has expanded overseas consultancy (offices/contracts in Saudi Arabia under an Aramco services agreement, UAE under an ADNOC framework agreement, a ~US$450mn PMC/EPCM contract for Dangote's Kenya refinery, ~Rs 730 crore Middle East contracts). FY25 consultancy-segment order book shows overseas backlog (~Rs 64,518 mn) exceeding domestic backlog (~Rs 40,463 mn), implying rising foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy was found.

FY25 revenue ~Rs 7,902 crore; domestic grew 16.4% YoY (~46% of revenue), international grew 20.5% YoY and contributed >54% of sales, split roughly Emerging Markets Rs 1,510 crore (+27.9%), Canada Rs 1,252 crore (+35.7%), Europe Rs 1,474 crore (+4.4%). Multi-currency export mix (CAD, EUR, and various EM currencies) implies material but not purely USD-denominated FX exposure; no specific hedging policy or USD-revenue % disclosed in sources reached (company also has operations in Vietnam and Dubai).

rural.evidence: Company commentary cites rural electrification and BharatNet rural-connectivity rollout as demand tailwinds for its electrical/communication cables sold through an extensive dealer network, but no revenue % specifically from rural markets is disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Commentary cites the government/PSU-led power-sector capex program (~Rs 3.12 lakh crore over 2 years for transmission upgradation, new substations, rural electrification) and Northeast India government infrastructure push as demand drivers for HV/EHV and electrical cables; no specific % of revenue from government/infra projects is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is widely reported as a zero-debt / net-cash balance sheet company, so floating-rate liability exposure appears minimal.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are copper (not crude-linked) and PVC compound/resin used for cable insulation (a petrochemical/crude derivative); FY25 standalone revenue was ~Rs 5,318.89 crore but no specific % of raw material cost tied to crude oil/PVC was found in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were under 2% of revenue in FY25 (export revenue rose from ~Rs 30 crore to ~Rs 52 crore, with a 2-3% export-share target over the next two years), so direct FX revenue exposure is limited; copper import costs may carry indirect USD linkage. No hedging policy was found in sources reached.

rural.evidence: Company is expanding beyond its Gurugram flagship into Tier-2 cities (Patna, Ranchi, Lucknow, Indore) and further planned sites (Guwahati, Varanasi, Mumbai, Pitampura, South Delhi, an Indore cancer unit), taking installed beds from ~3,665 toward ~7,000 over 3-4 years, broadening reach beyond metro markets; no explicit 'rural revenue %' figure is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-equity was low (~0.04) but rising after a large ~Rs 4,000 crore multi-year expansion capex program (Mumbai, Noida, bed-capacity additions), partly funded by debt alongside internal accruals; reported debt-equity rose to ~0.11 by FY26. Specific floating-vs-fixed-rate borrowing breakdown was not found in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: International (medical tourism) patients contribute ~7% of revenue, likely a multi-currency mix (Gulf/Africa/Bangladesh patients) rather than predominantly USD-denominated; no hedging policy disclosed in sources reached.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analyst/company commentary indicates Aether is systematically diversifying its raw-material sourcing across multiple geographies to reduce reliance on any single supplier and assure production continuity, positioning it to capture specialty-chemical/pharma-intermediate demand as global customers diversify away from China-concentrated supply. No AR text was directly readable in this session confirming management explicitly attributes revenue growth to China+1 in quantified terms, so rated moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Aether manufactures specialty/advanced intermediates and CDMO products; some inputs are petrochemical-derived, but no specific raw-material crude-linkage percentage was found in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (largely USD-denominated, per Q3 FY25 disclosure) was ~54.5% of total revenue vs. ~45.5% domestic; pharma vertical ~47.5% of revenue, agro ~11.2%, material science ~9.8% in Q3 FY25.

china_plus_one.evidence: IKS Health is a US-focused healthcare BPO/KPO (physician enablement platform) serving providers in the US, Canada and Australia; no manufacturing/export-goods supply chain, so China+1 dynamics are not applicable.

inr_exposure.evidence: Approximately 96% of IKS Health's revenue is derived from the United States (per IPO-time analysis); remainder from Canada/Australia. Company has been shifting delivery mix from onshore (US-based) to offshore (India-based) post the AQuity Solutions acquisition to improve margins, which also raises India-cost/USD-revenue currency mismatch exposure. No explicit hedging policy percentage found.

pli_scheme.evidence: IT/healthcare BPO services company; not a manufacturing entity and not part of any disclosed PLI sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/company commentary describes Privi as benefiting from 'China+1' tailwinds in aroma chemicals: stringent environmental norms and plant shutdowns in China/Europe have pushed global fragrance majors (who control ~2/3 of the global fragrance market) toward Indian suppliers like Privi, which backward-integrates Crude Sulphate Turpentine (CST) feedstock for cost/supply stability. Long-term contracts cover ~70% of sales. Not independently confirmed via direct AR text in this session, hence 'moderate' not 'strong'.

crude_exposure.evidence: Privi's primary feedstocks are Crude Sulphate Turpentine (CST, a paper/pulp-mill byproduct) and Gum Turpentine Oil (GTO), both pine-chemistry derived rather than petroleum-crude derived; some downstream chemistry also uses petrochemical derivatives. No specific % of raw materials linked to petroleum crude oil was found, so this is likely a weaker/indirect crude linkage than a typical petrochemical-feedstock exporter.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (Europe ~22%, North America ~15%, Asia ex-India ~16%, RoW ~11%, per Q3 FY25 investor presentation geography split) constitute ~70% of turnover (66% figure also cited for a more recent quarter), implying high foreign-currency revenue exposure. No explicit hedging % disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin Point is essentially a 100% export generics company (Latin America, Caribbean, Francophone Africa ~90% of revenue via emerging-market front-end model; US/regulated markets remainder). However, the specific growth strategy found involves partnering with Chinese API/ANDA holders to license products for LatAm filing (i.e., leveraging China, not diversifying away from it) plus a separate backward-integration push (target ~70% own-API for US filings via new Vizag/Chennai API facilities). This does not clearly match a 'customers shifting away from China' narrative, so rated weak rather than moderate/strong despite heavy export orientation.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company derives ~90% of revenue from emerging markets (Latin America, Caribbean, Africa) with remaining ~10-21% from the US/regulated markets (sources vary: 79%/21% and 90%/10% splits both cited); essentially all revenue is export/foreign-currency linked, though exact invoicing currency mix (USD vs local LatAm currencies) not confirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Castrol India is a domestic lubricants marketer (majority owned by BP) with no export/China+1 narrative found in accessible sources.

rural.evidence: Company has been pursuing a 'Bharat strategy' expanding direct distribution into feeder villages to capture rural two-wheeler, tractor and small-commercial-vehicle lubricant demand; management cites a 'rural-led recovery' in two-wheelers as part of its growth playbook (Autocar Professional interview, Apr 2026; Business Standard, Apr 2026: 'Castrol India banks on pricing, rural push to navigate cost pressures'). No specific revenue % from rural markets disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Base oil (a crude-oil derivative) is Castrol India's primary raw material; company explicitly states raw material costs depend on crude oil price movements and INR/USD movement, and imports the majority of its raw materials. Raw & packaging material cost was ~Rs 2,505.62 crore in CY2024. Falling Brent crude (range $75.4-$97.69/bbl vs $83.65-$114.75/bbl a year earlier) helped reduce raw/packaging material costs ~1.3% in a recent quarter. No exact % of COGS attributable to crude/base oil was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported to manage crude/currency volatility primarily through operational means (strategic sourcing, long-term supply contracts) rather than derivative/financial hedging instruments, per third-party analyst commentary; not independently verified against AR text.
inr_exposure.evidence: Castrol explicitly flags that continued crude oil price increases and rupee depreciation increase volatility in cost of goods; margin guidance held at 22-25% band despite lower crude, citing geopolitical uncertainty as an ongoing risk.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lubricants blending/marketing is not a PLI-covered sector for Castrol; no scheme participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Usha Martin operates manufacturing facilities in India, UK, Thailand and UAE (beyond a China-based footprint) and sells to 50+ countries; on a consolidated basis 35-40% of revenue is from exports to Europe, South East Asia, the US and Scandinavia (per FundsIndia equity research note). International markets were also cited as ~55% of FY25 consolidated revenue in one investor summary, reflecting demand from oil & gas, mining and infrastructure sectors abroad — but no AR text found explicitly framing this as 'China+1' order-win attribution, so classified moderate rather than strong. Note: the 55% vs 35-40% export figures conflict across sources, likely because consolidated 'international' revenue includes sales booked by overseas subsidiaries (UK/Thailand/UAE) in addition to direct exports from India; treat domestic/export split as approximate.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 commentary attributes international demand to oil & gas, mining and infrastructure sectors (cranes, ports, elevators use wire ropes), but no explicit % of revenue tied to government/infra capex was disclosed in sources reached.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~INR168 crore as of Dec 2024 (~28% of annualized operating EBITDA), indicating low overall leverage, but no floating-rate debt breakdown found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is steel wire rod, ~90-96% sourced captively from its own Usha Alloy Steel & Dredging (UASD) unit at Jamshedpur (integrated from iron ore/coal to wire rope), with 4-10% from other (incl. imported) sources. This is a steel/wire-rod cost exposure, not a direct crude-oil-linked raw material; company does sell wire ropes INTO the oil & gas sector as an end-market, which is a different (demand-side) exposure, not a raw-material one.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international revenue estimated 35-55% of consolidated revenue depending on source (see geography note); no specific hedging policy disclosure found in sources reached.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme relevant to wire rope/steel wire manufacturing found; not identified as a beneficiary of any PLI scheme in sources reached.

china_plus_one.evidence: HBL exports batteries/electronics via subsidiaries HBL America Inc. and HBL Germany GmbH, with named customers including Bombardier (Global 7500 aircraft), Siemens Germany (lithium-ion batteries for trains/metro cars), and defense customers in Israel and UAE (missile batteries). These are sole-source defense/aviation supply relationships, not a China+1 supply-chain-diversification narrative; no source found framing HBL's export growth in China+1 terms.

govt_capex.evidence: Significant railway/government exposure via Kavach (Train Collision Avoidance System) and railway signalling: recent single orders include a Rs 1,710 crore Kavach locomotive equipment modernization order, plus Rs 180 crore and Rs 132.95 crore railway contracts. One industry note states the Industrial Electronics segment (railway signalling, Kavach, Train Management Systems) grew from ~15% of revenue in FY25 to ~49% in FY26, indicating rising government/railway-capex linked revenue, though the FY25-specific % of total revenue from government/railway contracts was not precisely disclosed in sources reached.

crude_exposure.evidence: Core raw materials are lead, other battery chemistries (Ni-Cd, Silver-Zinc, Lithium) and electronics components — not directly crude-oil linked; no raw material cost % disclosed in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has export/foreign-currency revenue via US and German subsidiaries and defense exports to Israel/UAE, but no quantified USD/forex revenue % or hedging policy was found in sources reached.

pli_scheme.evidence: Under the PLI Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage, the awarded beneficiaries were Reliance New Energy Solar, Ola Electric Mobility, Hyundai Global Motors, and Rajesh Exports — HBL Engineering/HBL Power Systems is not among the named ACC PLI awardees found in government/PIB sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: APL Apollo is overwhelmingly domestic-focused: FY25 total sales volume was ~3.16 million tonnes, of which international/export business (including its Dubai plant) was only ~200-250kt (~6-8% of volume), up from ~110kt in FY24. No China+1 or export-diversification narrative found; growth strategy is centered on Indian infrastructure/construction demand. Domestic/export % here is estimated from sales VOLUME (tonnes), not confirmed revenue-value split.

rural.evidence: Some market commentary cites PMAY-Gramin (rural housing scheme, extended to FY29, targeting 2 crore additional rural houses) as a demand tailwind for structural steel tubes, but this appears in third-party market analysis rather than a company-disclosed rural revenue %.

govt_capex.evidence: Company/industry commentary cites Union Budget public capex (₹12.2 lakh crore proposed for FY26-27), new high-speed rail corridors, water infrastructure, oil/gas pipelines (national gas grid, city gas distribution) and PMAY housing as key demand drivers for structural steel tubes. Company's own FY26-28 capacity capex of ₹1,500 crore is being funded entirely via internal accruals (no new debt). No specific % of company revenue tied to government/infra orders was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company states planned FY26-28 expansion capex (~₹1,500 crore) will be funded entirely through internal accruals with no new debt, suggesting low incremental floating-rate debt reliance, but no existing floating-rate liability % was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material (HR Coil/steel) constitutes close to 90% of total operating cost; APL Apollo is India's largest buyer of HRC, sourcing >80% of steel from Tata Steel and JSW Steel (not vertically integrated). This is a steel/HRC price exposure, not a direct crude-oil-linked commodity, so left null for the crude-oil macro signal specifically.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share is small (~6-8% of volume in FY25); no forex hedging policy disclosure found in sources reached.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to structural steel tube manufacturing was identified; no beneficiary status found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent Pharma is primarily a branded-generics/formulations company (not a bulk-drug/API exporter), so the general pharma-industry China+1/API-diversification narrative (India reducing API import dependence on China) is less directly applicable to it. No company-specific China+1 statement was found in sources reached.

rural.evidence: Domestic (India) business is ~55% of consolidated revenue and the key growth driver; chronic and sub-chronic therapies (Cardiac, Anti-Diabetic, CNS, GI, Dermatology) account for ~77% of India sales. Company grew field force (medical representatives) to ~6,400 in FY25 (targeting 6,800-6,900 by FY26-end) to deepen territorial/regional reach, which may include semi-urban/rural expansion, but no explicit rural revenue % was disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company operations are exposed to foreign currency fluctuations from exports, imports and foreign-currency borrowings, mitigated via a stated comprehensive/near-100% hedging policy (per equity research commentary); not independently confirmed from primary AR text.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue break-up cited as India ~55%, Brazil ~10%, US ~10%, Germany ~10%, Other markets ~15% (source: brokerage/earnings summaries referencing Torrent's Q4 FY25 results). This gives multi-currency exposure to USD, BRL and EUR in addition to INR.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs has ~55 approved applicants; Torrent Pharmaceuticals was not specifically named among beneficiaries in government/press sources reached, but the full beneficiary list was not independently verified, so left null rather than false.

china_plus_one.evidence: Belrise (formerly Badve Engineering) is a domestic-anchored auto-component maker (2W frames/chassis, sheet metal, polymer parts) supplying 31+ OEMs including Hero MotoCorp, Royal Enfield, Honda; ~25% of FY25 revenue is international, including supply of 250+ components to Jaguar Land Rover's overseas plants in the UK, Austria and Slovakia as a single-source supplier. No China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found; export relationship appears OEM-program-driven (JLR) rather than China+1-driven.

rural.evidence: Two-wheeler (2W) segment is Belrise's largest business — 81.29% of manufacturing revenue and 64.65% of consolidated revenue in FY25. 2W demand in India is historically correlated with rural/semi-urban income and monsoon outcomes, but the company does not disclose a direct rural revenue split.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Pre-IPO borrowings were ~Rs 2,600 crore (as of Dec 2024); ~Rs 1,618.1 crore of May-2025 IPO proceeds were earmarked for debt reduction, bringing post-IPO debt/equity to a comfortable ~0.2:1 and lowering interest cost/rate sensitivity going forward. No floating-vs-fixed rate split was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Product portfolio spans metal (steel sheet metal/chassis/casting) and polymer components; polymer/plastic parts have an indirect petrochemical (crude-linked) input exposure, but no raw-material cost % breakdown was found in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~25% of FY25 revenue is international, with a notable single-source JLR supply relationship into UK/Austria/Slovakia plants (GBP/EUR exposure); no quantified USD-specific revenue % or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Auto Component PLI ('Champion OEM'/'Component Champion') scheme beneficiaries found in sources include Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Mitsubishi Electric, Toyota Kirloskar, Motherson Sumi, Bosch and Lucas-TVS; Belrise/Badve Engineering was not named in this (non-exhaustive, ~75-company) list, so beneficiary status is left null rather than false pending a primary-source check.
